chapter: Long Branch and the war years
title: Working at a hotel in Long Branch and living in Asbury Park, summer 1941
summary: The band played 8 to 12 at the Scarbourn Hotel; Phillips and Tex Briscoe lived in lively Asbury Park for 35 dollars more and commuted by train until Labor Day.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, we went up there, took six pieces up there, and stayed on this job. Had a helluva good job. Paid good money, and we went to work at 8 and got off at 12. We'd go around to all the beaches and all the clubs, and stay up til 5-6 o'clock in the morning, all around Asbury Park. That's where we stayed. That's where Tex and I stayed. The

rest of them stayed in a hotel. We was playing in a hotel, the Scarbourn Hotel. See, they'd give us rooms. You'd work the job for so much money, room and board. So Tex and I, we didn't want to stay out in Long Branch. We wanted to be where everything was happening, in Asbury Park. So the guy told us, "Well, if you all want to go, we'll give you thirty-five dollars more if you don't stay here." You know what I mean? On the salary. Well, that was good. We went and got us a room in Asbury Park, and we used to commute every day -- it wasn't but 6 miles. We'd catch a train. When we found out the way the trains were running...
You were talking about where the trains were running -- you found out about it.

Yeah. So we found out... We got off at 12 o'clock, and the train come by at 12:15, going back to Asbury Park. Then leaving Asbury Park in the evening, we could get a train out of there at 7 -- and we had to be at work at 8. It wasn't 6 miles. So we just commuted every day, and stayed over there where everything was happening. Wasn't nothin' happening out there in Long Branch. When you get through playing, it was dead. Wasn't nothin' too much there. But Asbury Park was jumpin'! They had a whole lot of clubs in
pAsbury Park. A lot of cats that I knew was playin' there, too.
How long did that gig last?
Oh, until the season -- Labor Day.
